mainTopic: Why impure תרומה oil may be burned for light on a weekday, the פסוקים permitting benefit while it burns, and whether 'ממנו' permits impure תרומה or impure קדשים.
overview: This amud opens with the end of an earlier argument: burning holy items cannot override יום טוב, because יום טוב is protected by both an עשה and a לא תעשה. The גמרא infers that lighting with impure תרומה oil is forbidden only on יום טוב, so on a weekday it is allowed, and it asks why. רב explains that impure תרומה must be burned, and the תורה lets you benefit from it while it burns. The גמרא brings two sources for this. The first is רב נחמן's reading of 'משמרת תרומותי … לך'. The second is רבי אבהו's reading of 'ולא בערתי ממנו בטמא'. The גמרא then argues over the word 'ממנו': does it permit impure תרומה or impure קדשים? A קל וחומר from מעשר seems to rule out קדשים, but the same logic would rule out תרומה too, and 'ממנו' must still permit something. The גמרא lists the חומרות of קדשים (פנ״ק עכ״ס) and then the חומרות of תרומה (מחפ״ז), and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: יום טוב has a positive and a negative command, so burning holy items cannot override it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier reasoning. יום טוב is protected by both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and a plain עשה, like burning holy leftovers, cannot push aside that double protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'שבתון' is a positive commandment to rest. So יום טוב has both a positive commandment and a prohibition. A positive commandment does not override a prohibition that comes together with a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the previous argument. It explains why you may not burn leftover or impure holy items on יום טוב, even though burning them is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning נותר or impure קדשים is only an עשה. Resting on יום טוב is protected by an עשה ('שבתון') and by a לא תעשה ('כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו'). The rule is that an עשה can never push aside a command that has both an עשה and a לא תעשה, so the burning must wait until after יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment (something you must do)

steps.confusionAlert: The first word 'עֲשֵׂה' is the end of a sentence earlier. That sentence said the word 'שבתון' is a positive command. It does not start a new idea.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step. If the reason for the ban is only the special status of יום טוב, then on a weekday there should be no problem.

phrases.english: is a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: End of the previous sentence: 'שבתון' is a positive command to rest.

phrases.english: And so a Festival becomes
a positive commandment and a prohibition —
phrases.notes: Both 'שבתון' and 'כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו'.

phrases.english: and a positive commandment does not override
a prohibition together with a positive commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם טוֹב עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the derivation earlier about why holy items are not burned on יום טוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Burning holy items, which is only an עשה, cannot override יום טוב, which has both an עשה and a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Inference that weekday lighting is allowed, and why
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that burning impure תרומה oil is forbidden only on יום טוב, so on a weekday it is fine. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is on יום טוב that it is forbidden. But on a weekday it is perfectly fine. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference and then asks a question. This sets up the next step, where רב explains why benefiting from impure תרומה is allowed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we might think impure תרומה is completely off-limits for any benefit. Yet the משנה only forbids lighting with it on יום טוב, which implies it is allowed during the week. The גמרא wants to know what source permits benefit from something that must be destroyed.

phrases.english: It is on a Festival that it is forbidden,
but on a weekday — it is perfectly fine.
phrases.notes: Inference from the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why may one benefit from impure תרומה?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הוּא דַּאֲסִיר, הָא בְּחוֹל שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the יום טוב reasoning and infers that weekdays are permitted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why may one benefit from impure תרומה oil on a weekday?

steps.title: רב: impure תרומה must be burned, and you may benefit while burning it
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that impure תרומה, like impure קדשים, must be burned. The תורה allows you to use it while it is being burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Just as there is a מצוה to burn holy items that became impure, so too there is a מצוה to burn תרומה that became impure. And the תורה said: while it is being destroyed, benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. Impure תרומה must be burned, and the תורה permits benefiting from it during that burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב compares impure תרומה to impure קדשים: both must be destroyed by burning. The new point is that for impure תרומה, the destruction itself may be done in a useful way, such as lighting a lamp. That is why weekday lighting is allowed, and only יום טוב is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
At the time of its destruction/burning

phrases.english: Rav said: Just as there is a מצוה
to burn consecrated items that became impure,
so too there is a מצוה to burn
teruma that became impure.
And the Torah said:
While it is being destroyed, benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּצְוָה לִשְׂרוֹף הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Impure תרומה must be burned, and the תורה permits benefit during its burning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the halachic basis for using impure תרומה oil for light on weekdays.

steps.title: Where does the תורה say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind רב's claim that the תורה permits benefit while burning impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did the תורה say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the פסוקים. This sets up the next steps, which bring two possible sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said 'the תורה said', but he did not quote a פסוק. The גמרא wants to know which verse teaches it.

phrases.english: Where did the Torah say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of רב's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that permits benefit from impure תרומה while it is burned.

steps.title: First source: 'תרומותי' means two kinds, and 'לך' means you may use it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, learns from 'משמרת תרומותי' (plural) that the פסוק covers pure and impure תרומה. The word 'לך' teaches that the impure kind is yours to burn under your cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: From רב נחמן's statement, quoting רבה בר אבוה: The פסוק says 'And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My תרומות.' The verse speaks of two תרומות: one pure and one impure. And רחמנא said 'to you': it shall be yours, to burn it under your cooked food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings its first source. The plural word 'תרומותי' includes impure תרומה, and 'לך' gives you the right to benefit from it by burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'תרומותי' (My terumot) hints at two kinds of תרומה, pure and impure. The pure kind is eaten. The impure kind cannot be eaten, so 'given to you' must mean a different benefit: using it as fuel under your pot.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (God, i.e., the תורה)
To use it as fuel / kindle it

phrases.english: From the statement of Rav Naḥman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: as Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The verse said:
"And I, behold, I have given you
the charge of My terumot" —
the verse is speaking of two terumot,
one, pure teruma,
and one, impure teruma.
And the Merciful One said: "to you" —
it shall be yours,
to burn it beneath your cooked dish.
phrases.notes: Benefit through burning, since eating is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 with a first פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תרומותי' includes impure תרומה, and 'לך' permits using it as fuel.

steps.title: Second source: 'I did not burn from it while impure'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, learns from וידוי מעשר: 'ממנו' (from מעשר) you may not burn while impure, but you may burn impure תרומה oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you like, say it comes from רבי אבהו's statement. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'Neither have I burned from it while impure.' From it you may not burn, but you may burn oil of תרומה that became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different source for the same law. It reads a limiting word in the פסוק of וידוי מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In וידוי מעשר, the farmer declares that he did not burn מעשר שני while impure. The word 'ממנו' (from it) limits the ban to מעשר. That implies that something else, impure תרומה oil, may be burned and used.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (an alternative answer)

steps.confusionAlert: 'ממנו' refers to מעשר שני, from the פסוק of וידוי מעשר. It does not refer to תרומה. The derashah works by contrast: מעשר is excluded, so תרומה is allowed.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is from Rabbi Abbahu's statement.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
"Neither have I destroyed from it while impure" —
from it you may not burn,
but you may burn
oil of teruma that became impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source to step 5 for the same law.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ממנו' excludes only מעשר, so impure תרומה oil may be burned.

steps.title: Challenge: maybe the exclusion permits impure holy oil instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second source. Why say 'ממנו' leaves room for impure תרומה? Maybe it leaves room for impure קדשים oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: from it you may not burn, but you may burn oil of קדשים that became impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אבהו's derashah. It argues that the word 'ממנו' could just as easily be permitting impure holy oil instead of impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ממנו' only tells us that something other than מעשר is permitted. It does not say what. The challenger suggests that the permitted item might be קדשים rather than תרומה, which would leave the derashah unable to prove רב's point.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (introduces an alternative reading)

phrases.english: But say: from it you may not burn,
but you may burn
oil of consecrated property that became impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִמֶּנּוּ אִי אַתָּה מַבְעִיר, אֲבָל אַתָּה מַבְעִיר שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנִּטְמָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's reading that 'ממנו' permits impure תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion is vague, so it could equally permit impure קדשים oil.

steps.title: Answer: a קל וחומר shows holy items are even stricter than מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר. If even lenient מעשר may not be burned while impure, stricter קדשים surely may not. So 'ממנו' must be permitting תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it a קל וחומר? If about מעשר, which is lenient, the תורה said 'I have not burned from it while impure', then קדשים, which are strict, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge with a קל וחומר. קדשים cannot be the permitted item, so the permitted item must be תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני has a lower level of holiness than קדשים. If the תורה forbids burning impure מעשר for benefit, then impure קדשים must certainly be forbidden, so 'ממנו' cannot be permitting קדשים. That leaves impure תרומה as the item 'ממנו' permits, so רבי אבהו's source seems to stand. The next step challenges this, because תרומה is also stricter than מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: An a fortiori argument (from lenient to strict)

steps.whatToRemember: Impure תרומה must be burned, and you may benefit from it while it burns, for example by lighting a lamp or cooking. This is learned from 'תרומותי/לך' or from 'ממנו' in וידוי מעשר. Lighting with it is forbidden only on יום טוב. The קל וחומר given here to rule out קדשים is challenged right away in the next steps.

phrases.english: Is it not an a fortiori inference?
If the tithe, which is lenient,
the Torah said:
"Neither have I destroyed from it while impure,"
consecrated items, which are stringent —
is it not all the more so?

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ממנו' might permit burning impure קדשים oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים are stricter than מעשר and are surely forbidden. So the exclusion permits impure תרומה.

steps.title: The same logic should forbid תרומה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר from Step 8. If that reasoning works, then תרומה, which is also stricter than מעשר, should be forbidden by the same קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then for תרומה too, let us say it is a קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the previous answer against itself. If a קל וחומר removes קדשים from 'ממנו', the same קל וחומר should remove תרומה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said: if lenient מעשר may not be burned while impure, stricter קדשים surely may not. But תרומה is also stricter than מעשר. So by the same logic, impure תרומה should be forbidden too, and then 'ממנו' would have nothing left to permit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It introduces a challenge built from the previous answer.
The portion of produce given to a כהן.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If you rely on a קל וחומר from מעשר.

phrases.english: teruma too,
let us say it is an a fortiori inference!
phrases.notes: תרומה is more severe than מעשר, so it should be forbidden too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, תְּרוּמָה נָמֵי לֵימָא קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר used as the answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from מעשר to קדשים in Step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר proves too much. It would forbid תרומה as well, leaving 'ממנו' with nothing to exclude.

steps.title: The word 'ממנו' must exclude something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק explicitly says 'ממנו', so something has to be excluded. The קל וחומר cannot cancel both options.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the extra word 'ממנו' guarantees that at least one thing is permitted. So the קל וחומר cannot wipe out both קדשים and תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר can tell us which item stays forbidden, but it cannot erase a word of the פסוק. Since 'ממנו' must teach something, one item must be permitted. This sets up the next question: which one?

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! It points to the wording of a פסוק as decisive.
From it. A limiting word in וידוי מעשר: from this item you may not burn, but other items you may.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the קל וחומר was wrong. It means the קל וחומר can apply to only one of the two items, because 'ממנו' must still leave one item permitted.

phrases.english: But it is written "from it"!
phrases.notes: The limiting word must exclude at least one item.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the explicit word of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר would forbid both קדשים and תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממנו' guarantees that one of the two is permitted. The קל וחומר can only forbid the other.

steps.title: Why choose תרומה over קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא demands a reason. Why decide that 'ממנו' permits תרומה and not קדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see? Why say תרומה is the item excluded?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that one item must be permitted, the גמרא asks what makes us pick תרומה. This short line sets up the debate in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both קדשים and תרומה are stricter than מעשר, so the קל וחומר alone does not decide between them. We need a reason why קדשים is the stricter one, so that it stays forbidden while תרומה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? It demands a reason for choosing one option over another.

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: Why exclude תרומה and not קדשים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 10. Since one item must be excluded, it asks which one and why.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'ממנו' excludes תרומה rather than קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both items are stricter than מעשר, so the choice of תרומה seems arbitrary.

steps.title: קדשים is stricter: six חומרות (פנ״ק עכ״ס)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it makes sense to keep קדשים forbidden, because קדשים has six חומרות that תרומה does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable that I do not exclude קדשים, since it has the חומרות remembered by the סימן פנ״ק עכ״ס: פיגול, נותר, קרבן, מעילה, כרת, and being forbidden to an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why קדשים stays forbidden. קדשים has many more serious laws than תרומה, so it is the stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item on the list applies to קדשים but not to תרומה. פיגול: an offering ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten. נותר: meat left past its time. קרבן: a sacrifice owed for eating קדשים while impure. מעילה: misusing holy property. כרת: the punishment for eating קדשים while impure. אונן: a mourner on the day of death may not eat קדשים. Since קדשים is so much stricter, 'ממנו' should be read as permitting the lighter item, תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable. A logical argument, not one drawn from a פסוק.
I exclude, I remove from the rule.
An offering ruined by an improper intention about when it will be eaten.
Meat of an offering left past its allowed time.
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial.

phrases.english: It is reasonable: I do not exclude consecrated items,
since (mnemonic) P-N-K, A-K-S applies to them:
phrases.notes: A memory aid. Each letter stands for one חומרה.

phrases.english: piggul, notar,
an offering, misuse of sacred property, and karet,
phrases.notes: The letters ק and ע stand for two separate items. Sefaria translates these together as 'קרבן מעילה'.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden to an acute mourner.
phrases.notes: The letter ס comes from אסור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by giving a reason to treat קדשים as stricter.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing the חומרות of the two items
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים has six חומרות that תרומה lacks, so it stays forbidden and 'ממנו' permits תרומה.

steps.title: On the contrary: תרומה has its own חומרות (מחפ״ז)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe תרומה should stay forbidden instead, because תרומה has חומרות that קדשים does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, I would not exclude תרומה, since it has the חומרות remembered by the סימן מחפ״ז: מיתה, חומש, and more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the argument and says תרומה might be the stricter one. It begins listing תרומה's own חומרות, and the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיתה: a non-כהן who eats תרומה on purpose is liable to death by the hand of Heaven. חומש: a non-כהן who eats it by accident pays its value plus an extra fifth. These laws are not found by קדשים in this way, so it is no longer clear which item is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary. It reverses the previous reasoning.
Death by the hand of Heaven, for a non-כהן who eats תרומה on purpose.
An added fifth, paid by a non-כהן who eats תרומה by accident.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
teruma is what I would not exclude,
since M-Ch-P-Z (mnemonic) applies to it:
death, one-fifth,
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 12's claim that קדשים is clearly the stricter item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 12 that קדשים is stricter than תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה has its own severe laws (מחפ״ז), so it could just as well be the item that stays forbidden.
